incidents.summary: Airtel was fined $8.3 million in Chad after a regulatory audit found that service quality fell below expected standards in 2022.

sources.title: $8.3 Million Fine Issued to Airtel from Chad for QoS - IT News Africa - African Business Technology News
sources.quote: Airtel Africa, a leading provider of telecommunications and mobile money services, with a presence in 14 countries in Africa, primarily East Africa and Central and West Africa, was recently issued a fine of $8.3 million by the Chadian government for failing to meet quality of service requirements.

incidents.summary: Airtel Money faced investigations over consumer complaints about opaque pricing and currency-conversion disclosures, including a COMESA probe initiated in January 2025.

sources.title: Airtel Africa plots H1 2026 IPO on the back of mobile money boom
sources.quote: Authorities in Kenya, Uganda, and Malawi have launched investigations following consumer complaints about opaque pricing and currency conversion disclosures.

sources.quote: In January 2025, the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) Competition Commission initiated a probe into Airtel Money’s pricing practices.

incidents.summary: COMESA opened an investigation into alleged anti-competitive conduct arising from Airtel Africa's 2022 tower partnership with American Tower Corporation.

sources.title: Regulator investigates ATC, Airtel Africa  - Developing Telecoms
sources.quote: The Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa competition commission opened an investigation into American Tower Corporation and Airtel Africa, for alleged anti-competitive conduct, after the two companies signed a partnership agreement in 2022.

sources.title: Regulator investigates ATC, Airtel Africa  - Developing Telecoms
sources.quote: COMESA received a complaint alleging the existence of anti-competitive agreements between ATC and Airtel Africa, in which Airtel will take a certain number of ATC sites annually and in return, ATC will give a cash rebate to Airtel.

positives: Airtel Africa converted 390 off-grid sites to grid power in 2025/26 and reduced diesel consumption through power and cooling upgrades.
Airtel Africa recycled 94% of operational waste during its 2025/26 financial year.
Through its UNICEF partnership, Airtel Africa connected 3,296 schools to free internet, reaching over two million learners and 38,868 teachers.
